title: Cousins Allen and Clyde drank themselves to death
summary: Cousin Allen, a trombonist with Lionel Hampton, died of wine and Clyde, the tuba player, followed within months.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Listen, while we're just thinking. I just try to remember things as they come back in my mind. I thought that was kind of touching, what you said about the cousins. Well, first of all you said everybody drank. You said practically everyone in the family did some drinking.
The two cousins drink themselves to death.
What. The two cousins did drink themselves to death.

Sure, Allen was drinking so. In '48 I went to California and he was playing and had just left Lionel Hampton, and they gave him a job in Chicago as a D.J. and he wrote me out here -- now, this is late -- that was in '48.
Now, wait a minute, what was his instrument.
Lionel Hampton, played with Lionel Hampton, Allen Barry (phonetic). Kind of light complected boy, very nice looking boy, had that old drinking look though.
That old drinking look, and he went out to the West Coast and then they brought him to Chicago.

Yeah, and then he went to the West Coast and when I was out there with the Ink Spots he was out there and a lot of people say, man, Allen still playing but he drinking. He's drinking so much. I went down to see him, yeah, yeah, I'm going to quit. I'm going to quit, yeah, I know. Make me sick. I ain't going to drink no more, I'm going to quit, but he didn't. He went to Chicago and he wrote me and the next thing I heard, the wine killed him.

And then the other brother, he started drinking because it was so close, they favored each other -- Clyde, the oldest one, they say he died six months after, grieved himself to death. Started drinking heavy too. He drank whiskey.
Bass. That's all he ever played, was the bass fiddle. Bass horn, I meant to say.
Oh, the bass horn, the tuba you mean.
The tuba, that's what he played.

He played with Gene Coy's Black Aces and he stayed with them a lot of years, I guess, and Gene Coy. That's the same, Gene Coy's Black Aces and he might have played with somebody else and then he played with us.
